intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the phenomenon while waiting for the lights to dance overhead.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool surrounded by black lava fields. The mineral-rich waters average 38–40°C and are renowned for skin benefits. Upgrade options include in-water massages and a lava restaurant meal. Book well in advance as slots sell out fast.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 set in a stunning geothermal landscape with bubbling geysers nearby. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, it offers an authentic and affordable hot spring experience surrounded by steaming vents and wild scenery.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food Walk & Viking Culture Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's culinary scene and Viking heritage on a guided walking tour through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fermented shark (hákarl), and fresh langoustine. Visit the Settlement Exhibition museum built over actual Viking-age ruins discovered beneath the city.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's dramatic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands to reach the legendary Landmannalaugar natural hot spring. Hike across obsidian lava fields and steaming fumaroles before rewarding yourself with a long soak in the natural geothermal pool. One of Iceland's most surreal and unforgettable landscapes.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Flybus (around 3,500 ISK) to Reykjavik. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Take a short walk along the nearby shoreline to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Head into central Reykjavik for a first exploration. Walk along Laugavegur street, visit Hallgrimskirkja church exterior (free), and watch for northern lights after dark from the beachfront near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at Keflavik Airport
meals.lunch: Pick up groceries at Bonus supermarket (Iceland's most budget-friendly chain) near the city center for self-catering essentials
meals.dinner: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall - try a budget bowl from one of the vendors (around 2,000-2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January means very limited daylight (roughly 5-6 hours). Darkness falls around 17:00, which is ideal for northern lights hunting. Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) for aurora forecasts. Stock up at Bonus supermarket to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportid) if open on weekends, or explore the Old Harbour area. Walk to the Sun Voyager sculpture (free) along the waterfront promenade for iconic coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Reykjavik on foot: visit Tjornin lake (free), the colorful corrugated iron houses of the old town, and the exterior of Harpa Concert Hall. Browse the free exhibits at the Culture House or sit in Hallgrimskirkja church interior (free entry to the nave).
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt from the Grotta Lighthouse area near the hotel - one of the best spots near Reykjavik for aurora viewing with minimal light pollution. Bring warm layers and a thermos of hot drink.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel using groceries from Bonus - oatmeal, yogurt, and fruit
meals.lunch: Bajarins Beztu Pylsur - Iceland's famous hot dog stand, one hot dog costs around 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel - pasta or soup from Bonus groceries

day_by_day.notes: Check the aurora forecast on the Vedur app each evening. A KP index of 3 or above with clear skies gives good viewing chances. January nights are long (18+ hours of darkness), maximizing aurora opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Golden Circle. Rent a budget car (pre-book online for best rates, around 8,000-10,000 ISK/day) or join a budget group tour. Start at Thingvellir National Park - walk the Almannagjá gorge (free entry) and see the continental rift between Eurasian and North American tectonic plates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Geysir geothermal area to watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes (free entry to the area). Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall - one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, free to view from the path.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by 17:00. After dark, drive or walk to a dark spot near the hotel for northern lights viewing. The Grótta peninsula is excellent.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel - bread, cheese, and coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a self-made sandwich from Bonus groceries to eat at Thingvellir or Geysir
meals.dinner: Aktu Taktu burger restaurant in Reykjavik - budget-friendly Icelandic fast food (around 2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip. Road conditions in January can be icy - always check road.is before driving. Car rental includes winter tires by law in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula. Drive to the Bridge Between Continents (free) - a small footbridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Explore the dramatic lava fields and volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse and Valahnukamol cliffs for dramatic ocean views. Explore the geothermal area at Gunnuhver - Iceland's largest hot spring (free access). Steam vents and boiling mud pools create an otherworldly scene.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel. Check aurora forecast and head to Grotta Lighthouse or the hotel beachfront for northern lights viewing with hot drinks.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel - eggs, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel - wraps and fruit from Bonus
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel - Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) made from ingredients bought at Bonus, a warming winter meal

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver hot springs are free but stay on marked paths - the ground around geothermal areas can be dangerously thin. The Reykjanes Peninsula is easily accessible from Reykjavik and the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Seltjarnarnes peninsula near the hotel for a morning coastal walk. Explore the bird cliffs and sea views. On clear days you can see Snæfellsjökull glacier across the bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget dip at Vesturbæjarlaug - one of Reykjavik's neighborhood geothermal swimming pools (entry around 1,000 ISK). These local pools are heated by geothermal energy and are a beloved Icelandic tradition, far cheaper than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's street art scene - the city has an impressive collection of murals around the downtown area. After dark, head to Öskjuhlíd hill (Pearl building area) for a dark sky northern lights spot within the city.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel - skyr (Icelandic yogurt) with granola
meals.lunch: Noodle Station in Reykjavik - excellent budget noodle soup for around 1,800 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel - baked fish with vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic geothermal pools are a must-do cultural experience. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The pools are used by locals year-round regardless of weather and are far more affordable than tourist-focused hot spring experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip south along the Ring Road. Drive to Seljalandsfoss waterfall (parking fee around 800 ISK) - you can walk behind this waterfall. Note: the path behind may be icy in January, exercise caution.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skogafoss waterfall (free) - one of Iceland's most impressive falls. Climb the 527 steps to the viewing platform for panoramic views. Drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara (free) - dramatic basalt columns and sea stacks, but respect the dangerous waves.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Reykjavik. Stop at Hvolsvollur or Selfoss for fuel and snacks. Back at hotel, check aurora forecast for evening viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel - packed and ready for early departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Skogafoss or Reynisfjara beach
meals.dinner: Kronan supermarket grab-and-go or self-catered at hotel upon return

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day drive (approximately 350 km round trip). Reynisfjara beach is beautiful but extremely dangerous - sneaker waves have killed tourists. Never turn your back on the ocean. Check road.is for conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the long driving day. Sleep in, have a leisurely breakfast, and do laundry if needed. Visit the nearby Seltjarnarnes geothermal hot pot (free outdoor hot pot) for a relaxing morning soak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (entry around 2,500 ISK) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history and culture. Alternatively, visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnamssyningin) which displays Viking-age ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free northern lights walking tour from central Reykjavik (many hostels and guesthouses offer these). Alternatively, take a self-guided drive to Hafnarfjordur lava park for dark sky aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered leisurely breakfast at hotel - pancakes or eggs
meals.lunch: Grái Kötturinn cafe in Reykjavik - cozy budget-friendly cafe with soups and sandwiches (around 1,500-2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel - Icelandic fish stew using fresh fish from Bonus

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for budget travelers to recover energy and save money with self-catered meals. The free outdoor hot pot at Seltjarnarnes is a hidden gem known mostly to locals.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (long day, approximately 350 km round trip). Depart early. Drive north along Route 1 and then west. Stop at Borgarnes Settlement Center exterior and the scenic Hvalfjordur fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsnes: visit Kirkjufell mountain (free viewpoint) - one of Iceland's most photographed peaks. Continue to Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal walk (free) with dramatic lava arch formations and bird cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik as darkness falls. The remote location of Snæfellsnes offers excellent northern lights viewing on the return journey if skies are clear - pull over safely on the roadside.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Kirkjufell or Arnarstapi
meals.dinner: Grab food at a petrol station N1 or Olís on the return route (budget hot dogs and soup available)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a long but spectacular day trip. The peninsula inspired Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth. Road conditions in January can be challenging - check road.is. Consider starting by 08:00 to maximize limited daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Laugardalur valley in Reykjavik - walk around the botanical garden (free in winter) and the large geothermal Laugardalslaug swimming complex (entry around 1,000 ISK). This is Reykjavik's largest public pool with hot tubs and steam rooms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Elliðaár valley nature reserve within Reykjavik (free) - a surprisingly wild river valley with walking trails. Visit the Árbær Open Air Museum (check winter hours, entry around 1,800 ISK) for historical Icelandic turf houses.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt from Öskjuhlíd hill near the Pearl building - one of the best in-city dark spots. Bring a blanket and thermos. Check aurora forecast - January statistically has high aurora activity.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch in Laugardalur park
meals.dinner: Pylsuvagninn - another famous hot dog cart in Reykjavik, budget-friendly (under 1,000 ISK for a meal)

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug pool is a fantastic budget experience. Locals use it daily and it costs a fraction of commercial hot spring experiences. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Hengill geothermal area. Drive to Nesjavellir geothermal power plant area (free to view from outside) and walk the free hiking trails through steaming vents and colorful geothermal ground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Thingvallavatn lake - Iceland's largest natural lake, located in Thingvellir National Park (free entry). Walk the free trails around the lake shore. In summer you can snorkel here but in January enjoy the dramatic winter landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by 17:00. Evening aurora hunt from Thingvellir on the return if skies are clear - the national park has very dark skies and is excellent for aurora photography.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Nesjavellir or Thingvellir
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel - hearty Icelandic lamb chops from Bonus supermarket

day_by_day.notes: The Hengill geothermal area is free and less touristy than Geysir. Steam rises dramatically from the ground creating an alien landscape. Stay on marked paths - geothermal ground can be unstable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark. Drive to Kleifarvatn lake - a mysterious dark lake with geothermal activity on its shores (free). Walk the lava field paths around the lake for dramatic volcanic scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Krysuvík geothermal area (free) - colorful boiling mud pools, steaming vents, and sulfur deposits create a surreal landscape. Drive along the Reykjanes coast to the Bridge Between Continents area for a different perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel. This is your second-to-last full evening - make it count for northern lights. Head to Grotta Lighthouse for a dedicated 2-hour aurora watch session with a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel - bigger breakfast to fuel the day
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Kleifarvatn lake
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner - Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) in Reykjavik Old Harbour for lobster soup (around 2,500 ISK) - a budget splurge worth it

day_by_day.notes: Krysuvík is one of Iceland's most impressive free geothermal areas. The colors of the sulfur deposits are extraordinary. Boardwalks are in place but can be icy in January - wear grippy boots.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day. Visit the Perlan museum (exterior and free viewing deck is accessible, or pay for the Northern Lights planetarium show inside for around 2,900 ISK - a good budget option to guarantee a northern lights experience regardless of weather).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Kolaportid flea market or Bonus/Kronan for budget Icelandic food souvenirs (skyr, licorice, dried fish). Visit Tjornin lake one final time and walk the city center streets.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights hunt - this is your last chance. Take a taxi or drive to a dark location outside the city. If aurora is not visible, the Perlan Northern Lights show in the morning would have been a good backup. Celebrate the trip with a final Icelandic dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel - use up remaining groceries
meals.lunch: Sandwich from Bonus or a local bakery (Braud & Co for fresh Icelandic pastries, around 500-800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Final dinner treat - Icelandic Fish & Chips in Reykjavik Old Harbour (around 2,500-3,000 ISK) for authentic Icelandic flavors

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags tonight for early departure tomorrow. Leave a review for the hotel. Budget summary: aim to keep daily spending under 8,000-10,000 ISK (excluding accommodation and car rental) by self-catering most meals.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Load luggage and drive to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Allow extra time for winter road conditions and airport security.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavik Airport. Arrive at least 2.5-3 hours before flight for international departures. Browse duty-free for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs (Brennivín schnapps and Icelandic chocolate are affordable options).
day_by_day.evening: Flight departs. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Iceland - northern lights, hot springs, waterfalls, glaciers, and volcanic landscapes explored on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before checkout - use up any remaining food
meals.lunch: Airport food or pack remaining snacks from hotel
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car with a full tank (fill up before the airport as airport fuel is more expensive). The Flybus back to the airport costs around 3,500 ISK if you did not rent a car. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases over 6,000 ISK at tourist shops.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the phenomenon while waiting for the lights to dance overhead.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool surrounded by black lava fields. The mineral-rich waters average 38–40°C and are renowned for skin benefits. Upgrade options include in-water massages and a lava restaurant meal. Book well in advance as slots sell out fast.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 set in a stunning geothermal landscape with bubbling geysers nearby. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, it offers an authentic and affordable hot spring experience surrounded by steaming vents and wild scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in. Take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to get oriented and enjoy the dramatic Icelandic coastal scenery. Visit a nearby geothermal pool or hotel hot tub to recover from the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — join the small-group guided jeep tour departing from the resort area into the dark countryside away from light pollution. January offers long dark nights, maximizing aurora viewing chances.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside café en route to the resort — try a traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) at a local diner (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant before the Northern Lights tour — opt for pan-seared Arctic char with roasted root vegetables (~4,500–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January darkness is ideal for Northern Lights viewing. Keep aurora forecast apps (Vedur.is) handy. Dress in thermal layers — temperatures can be -5°C to 5°C. The jeep tour typically runs 21:00–01:00.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from the late Northern Lights tour. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Afterward, take a scenic morning drive along the Reykjanes Peninsula coastal roads, stopping at dramatic sea cliffs and lava fields near the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — spend the afternoon soaking in Iceland's iconic milky-blue geothermal pools surrounded by black lava fields. The mineral-rich waters are especially magical in the January mist. Book the Comfort Package in advance (~12,000–14,000 ISK) which includes silica mud mask and algae mask.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and early bedtime to reset your sleep schedule after Day 1's late night.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at the resort — skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, and eggs (~2,000–3,000 ISK or included with stay)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant — enjoy a lighter menu option such as the fish of the day or Icelandic vegetable soup (~3,500–5,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at a local restaurant near the resort — try Icelandic lamb chops with mashed turnips and berry sauce (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in peak aurora season (Jan–Mar). Bring a waterproof hair tie and avoid wearing jewelry in the silica-rich water.

day_by_day.morning: Drive toward the Golden Circle route. Begin at Þingvellir National Park — walk the dramatic Almannagjá gorge where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. In January, the frozen landscape adds an ethereal quality to the site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to Geysir Geothermal Area — watch the famous Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Stroll the surrounding bubbling mud pools and fumaroles.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Gullfoss Waterfall — Iceland's most iconic waterfall, partially frozen in January with ice formations framing the cascading water. Return to resort in the evening. Check aurora forecast for a potential spontaneous viewing from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch at Geysir Center café — lamb stew or fish and chips (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friðheimar — a unique greenhouse restaurant near Gullfoss serving tomato-based dishes grown on-site, including tomato soup and fresh bread (~3,500–4,500 ISK). Reservation recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle roads are generally well-maintained but can be icy in January. Rent a 4WD vehicle if not already arranged. Daylight in January is limited to roughly 5–6 hours (11:00–16:00), so plan outdoor sightseeing tightly within daylight windows.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891. Arrive early morning when crowds are thinner. The natural hot spring sits at a perfect 38–40°C and is surrounded by geothermal activity including a small geyser that erupts regularly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Flúðir village area and nearby geothermal greenhouse farms. Drive back toward the South Coast, stopping at Kerið Volcanic Crater — a striking red-walled crater lake, often partially frozen in January creating a stunning blue-white contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (second opportunity) — take advantage of another guided jeep excursion for a second chance at aurora viewing with expert guides who track real-time forecasts.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the drive to Flúðir
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch from a local supermarket (Krónan or Bónus) — Icelandic skyr, rye bread, and smoked lamb (~1,000–1,500 ISK). Eat at the Secret Lagoon parking area.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort or a nearby South Coast restaurant — grilled cod with butter sauce and potatoes (~3,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon admission is approximately 3,000 ISK per adult. Bring your own towel or rent one on-site. The lagoon is outdoors so the contrast of cold January air and warm water is invigorating. Swimwear is required.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the South Coast toward Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most photogenic falls where you can walk behind the cascading curtain of water. In January, ice formations on the rocks create a magical frozen fairy-tale scene. Note: the path behind the falls may be closed if icy — check conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall — a powerful 60-meter-wide waterfall. Climb the 370 steps to the viewing platform for panoramic South Coast views. Explore the nearby Skógar Folk Museum to learn about traditional Icelandic turf house life.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Vík village — Iceland's southernmost village with dramatic black sand beaches and basalt sea stacks (Reynisdrangar). Enjoy the moody coastal atmosphere at dusk. Return to resort or stay overnight in Vík (optional upgrade night).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skógarfoss area café or food truck — lamb soup or fish sandwich (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Halldórskaffi in Vík — a cozy local restaurant serving Icelandic comfort food including lamb stew and fresh fish (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves — never turn your back to the ocean and stay well back from the waterline. January conditions can be very windy on the South Coast. Wear windproof outer layers.

day_by_day.morning: If staying in Vík, drive to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — a breathtaking glacial lake filled with floating icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier. In January, the lagoon may have ice floes and the lighting is dramatic even in limited daylight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Diamond Beach adjacent to Jökulsárlón — where translucent ice chunks wash ashore on black volcanic sand, sparkling like diamonds. Explore the area and photograph the surreal landscape. Visit the nearby Fjallsárlón Glacier Lagoon for a quieter alternative viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive toward the resort. Stop at a geothermal hot pot along the route if time permits. Check aurora forecast — the open South Coast offers excellent dark skies for aurora viewing from the car or roadside.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Vík accommodation or a local bakery
meals.lunch: Café at Jökulsárlón visitor center — lamb soup and bread (~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant in Kirkjubæjarklaustur on the return route — grilled Icelandic trout or lamb burger (~3,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 375 km from Reykjavik — a long but rewarding day trip. Consider splitting this into an overnight stay in the area to reduce driving pressure. Road conditions on Route 1 (Ring Road) can be challenging in January — always check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day at the resort. Enjoy the resort's hot spring or pool facilities. Take a slow morning with a long breakfast and relaxation — essential for a balanced trip pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula more deeply — visit the Bridge Between Continents (a small footbridge symbolizing the gap between tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver hot spring area with its powerful steam vents, and the Reykjanesviti Lighthouse (Iceland's oldest lighthouse).
day_by_day.evening: Reykjavik city evening — drive 45 minutes into the capital. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church exterior (illuminated at night), stroll Laugavegur shopping street for window browsing, and enjoy dinner in the city.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop at a petrol station café — Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) with all toppings, a beloved local tradition (~500–800 ISK at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Reykjavik — try Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) for fresh lobster soup and grilled fish skewers in a casual harbour-side setting (~3,000–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hallgrímskirkja's tower offers panoramic city views during opening hours (usually 09:00–17:00 in winter). Laugavegur has excellent local shops for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa) and souvenirs. Parking in Reykjavik city center is metered.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Reykjavik. Morning visit to the National Museum of Iceland — explore 1,200 years of Icelandic history from Viking settlement to modern times. Excellent indoor activity for a cold January morning (~2,000 ISK entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront — the stunning geometric glass facade is particularly beautiful in winter light. Walk the Old Harbour area and visit the Whales of Iceland exhibition (life-size whale models, ~3,500 ISK). Browse the weekend flea market at Kolaportið if open.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 16:00) at Perlan — the futuristic dome building offering 360° panoramic views over Reykjavik and the surrounding mountains and ocean. Visit the Wonders of Iceland exhibition inside. Dinner in the city before returning to resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before driving to Reykjavik
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic open-faced sandwiches (smørrebrød) with smoked lamb and herring, plus fermented shark for the adventurous (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Matur og Drykkur — a celebrated restaurant serving creative modern Icelandic cuisine based on traditional recipes (~5,000–7,000 ISK per person, splurge-worthy)

day_by_day.notes: Perlan's observation deck is free; the Wonders of Iceland museum inside has a separate entry fee (~3,500 ISK). The indoor ice cave exhibit at Perlan is a highlight. Book dinner reservations in advance for popular Reykjavik restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north toward Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2 hours from the resort). Stop at Deildartunguhver — Europe's most powerful hot spring, with water at 97°C gushing at 180 liters per second. The steam clouds are dramatic in cold January air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the dramatic Lóndrangar basalt sea stacks. The snowy volcanic peak visible on clear days is stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Kirkjufell Mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain, especially magical in winter with snow and potential aurora reflections in the stream in front. Check aurora forecast for evening viewing from this iconic spot.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the long drive
meals.lunch: Lunch in Borgarnes — stop at the Settlement Center café for Icelandic lamb soup and fresh bread (~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Grundarfjörður near Kirkjufell — local restaurant serving fresh fish caught from the surrounding fjords (~3,500–4,500 ISK). Consider overnight stay in Snæfellsnes to avoid long return drive.

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes Peninsula is approximately 200 km from the resort — a full-day commitment. Roads in the peninsula can be challenging in January. An overnight stay in Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur is recommended to fully enjoy this region without rushing.

day_by_day.morning: If staying overnight on Snæfellsnes: morning visit to Stykkishólmur — a charming fishing town with colorful houses. Visit the Library of Water art installation and the historic Norwegian House museum. Walk to the hilltop lighthouse for fjord views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward the resort via Route 54. Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Húsafell — a series of rivulets cascading over ancient lava fields into the Hvítá river, often partially frozen in January creating extraordinary ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the resort's hot spring or geothermal pool for a relaxing evening soak. Early dinner and rest after two days of extensive driving.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Stykkishólmur guesthouse or local bakery
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from a local supermarket eaten near Hraunfossar waterfalls
meals.dinner: Comfort dinner at the resort — Icelandic meat soup (kjötsúpa) or pan-fried haddock (~3,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hraunfossar is a hidden gem often missed by tourists — the lava-filtered waterfalls are unique in Iceland. The drive back from Snæfellsnes through the Dalir region offers beautiful fjord and mountain scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort. Enjoy the beachfront scenery and resort amenities. Optional: visit a local geothermal community pool (sundlaug) near the resort — Icelanders' beloved daily ritual, featuring hot pots at various temperatures, steam rooms, and cold plunge pools (~1,000 ISK entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark — explore the Eldvörp lava field, Seltún geothermal area with its colorful sulfur deposits and bubbling mud pools, and the dramatic coastal cliffs at Hafnaberg where birds nest in summer (empty but scenic in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (third opportunity) — take the guided jeep tour for a last dedicated aurora hunting session. January's long nights and frequent aurora activity make this a prime opportunity. Celebrate with warm cocoa provided by guides.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local café in Grindavík town near the resort — fish stew and fresh bread (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at the resort — grilled lamb with roasted vegetables and Icelandic butter (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Seltún geothermal area is a smaller, less crowded alternative to Geysir with equally impressive sulfurous activity. Wooden boardwalks protect the fragile geothermal crust — stay on marked paths. The colors of the mineral deposits (orange, yellow, green) are vivid even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit the Blue Lagoon for a second, more leisurely soak now that you know the layout. Alternatively, visit the nearby Lava Center in Hvolsvöllur — an excellent interactive museum about Iceland's volcanic activity with earthquake simulators and eruption films.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and final exploration. Visit Reykjavik's Laugavegur street for Icelandic wool products, local design items, and food gifts (skyr, Icelandic salt, dried fish, schnapps). Visit the Kolaportið flea market if it's a weekend.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Reykjavik — celebrate the trip with a special meal. Enjoy a sunset/twilight walk along the Seltjarnarnes peninsula waterfront near Reykjavik for a final view of the ocean and mountains. Return to resort for final packing.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Reykjavik's Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) — Icelandic beef burger or fish of the day in a lively atmosphere (~3,500–5,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) — elegant Icelandic-Asian fusion seafood in Reykjavik's old town (~5,500–8,000 ISK per person — a fitting splurge for the last night)

day_by_day.notes: Pack Icelandic food gifts carefully — dried fish and certain meat products may have customs restrictions when returning to home countries. Check airline baggage allowances for heavy wool sweater purchases. Settle any outstanding resort bills this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Enjoy a final Icelandic breakfast at the resort. Check out and load the vehicle. Drive to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 20–40 minutes from the resort depending on exact location). Return rental car if applicable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport check-in and departure procedures. Keflavik Airport has excellent duty-free shopping — Icelandic spirits (Brennivín schnapps), Icelandic chocolate, and beauty products from the Blue Lagoon brand make excellent last-minute purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Northern Lights, geothermal hot springs, dramatic waterfalls, glaciers, and the unique magic of Iceland in winter.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor Icelandic skyr and smoked salmon one last time
meals.lunch: Lunch at Keflavik Airport — Icelandic fish and chips or a bowl of lamb soup at one of the airport restaurants (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Meal on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport check-in, security, and duty-free browsing. Keflavik Airport is modern and efficient but can be busy in peak aurora season. Keep aurora photos and memories — Iceland in January is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the phenomenon while waiting for the lights to dance overhead.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool surrounded by black lava fields. The mineral-rich waters average 38–40°C and are renowned for skin benefits. Upgrade options include in-water massages and a lava restaurant meal. Book well in advance as slots sell out fast.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 set in a stunning geothermal landscape with bubbling geysers nearby. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, it offers an authentic and affordable hot spring experience surrounded by steaming vents and wild scenery.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food Walk & Viking Culture Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's culinary scene and Viking heritage on a guided walking tour through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fermented shark (hákarl), and fresh langoustine. Visit the Settlement Exhibition museum built over actual Viking-age ruins discovered beneath the city.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's dramatic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands to reach the legendary Landmannalaugar natural hot spring. Hike across obsidian lava fields and steaming fumaroles before rewarding yourself with a long soak in the natural geothermal pool. One of Iceland's most surreal and unforgettable landscapes.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeur transfer from Keflavik Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 45–60 min). Check-in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity from the resort. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to acclimate to Iceland's winter atmosphere and stunning coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: First taste of Iceland's premium culinary scene with dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Afterward, step outside for an informal first attempt at spotting the Northern Lights from the resort's private beachfront — no tour tonight, just a relaxed introduction to Iceland's magical skies.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining prior to arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and Icelandic open-faced sandwiches (smørrebrød-style) at the resort lounge upon check-in
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring Icelandic lamb, Arctic char, and locally foraged ingredients paired with a curated Icelandic wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. January days in Iceland are very short (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~15:30), so the afternoon arrival already means near-darkness. Pack layers for the evening stroll. Check in early if possible to maximize rest after the flight.

day_by_day.morning: Slow luxury morning at the resort — enjoy a lavish Icelandic breakfast buffet featuring skyr, smoked salmon, fresh rye bread, and Icelandic cheeses. Attend a brief resort orientation and plan the week ahead with your dedicated concierge. Relax in the resort's private hot tub or indoor heated pool overlooking the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa experience (pre-booked Premium or Retreat package). Soak in Iceland's world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters surrounded by dramatic black lava fields. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and algae masks included in the premium package. Sip Icelandic sparkling wine at the in-water bar.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head out for the Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — a small-group guided excursion into the dark Icelandic countryside away from light pollution. Expert guides track aurora forecasts in real time to maximize sighting chances. Return to the resort by approximately 23:00.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic luxury breakfast buffet at the resort — skyr parfaits, smoked lamb, Icelandic rye bread, fresh pastries, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — a premium dining experience overlooking the geothermal waters, featuring Icelandic seafood chowder, langoustine, and volcanic bread
meals.dinner: Light post-Northern Lights supper at the resort's lounge bar — Icelandic lamb sliders, cheese boards, and hot chocolate with Icelandic schnapps (brennivín)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be pre-booked well in advance — Retreat Spa package recommended for full luxury experience. Northern Lights tour typically departs around 21:00. Dress in thermal layers under the provided jeep blankets. Aurora activity depends on geomagnetic conditions (Kp index).

day_by_day.morning: Guided Reykjavik Food Walk & Viking Culture Tour — explore Reykjavik's culinary scene and Viking heritage on a private guided walking tour through the city center. Visit Hallgrímskirkja Church, the harbor, and hidden foodie gems. Sample traditional Icelandic bites including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, and lamb soup.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik independently — visit the Harpa Concert Hall for its stunning glass architecture, browse the Laugavegur shopping street for premium Icelandic wool (lopapeysa sweaters) and design goods. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for deep Viking history immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Reykjavik's top fine-dining establishments followed by a return to the resort. Optional second Northern Lights alert — the resort concierge will notify you if aurora activity is high, allowing for a spontaneous beachfront viewing session.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Icelandic waffles with crowberry jam, smoked salmon platters, and freshly brewed Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Tasting stops included on the Reykjavik Food Walk — traditional lamb soup (kjötsúpa), skyr desserts, and artisan Icelandic bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant (Reykjavik's Michelin-starred New Nordic cuisine) — seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing featuring Icelandic ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Private car or luxury taxi recommended for Reykjavik transfers (~45 min from resort). Dill Restaurant reservations must be made months in advance — ensure concierge books ahead. January walking tours are cold — full thermal gear essential.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort — indulge in a spa treatment (hot stone massage or geothermal facial using Icelandic mineral products). Enjoy the resort's private beachfront in the soft winter morning light for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided Golden Circle tour — visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site, tectonic plate boundary), the erupting Geysir geothermal area (watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes), and the majestic Gullfoss waterfall partially frozen in winter glory.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the Golden Circle in time for sunset/dusk photography at Gullfoss before heading back. Dinner at the resort followed by a Northern Lights watch from the private beachfront with a glass of Icelandic gin and tonic.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — skyr bowls with Icelandic berries, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Gullfoss Café or a pre-packed luxury picnic hamper prepared by the resort with Icelandic cheeses, smoked meats, and thermos of lamb soup
meals.dinner: Multi-course dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — Arctic char en croûte, reindeer tenderloin, and Icelandic cheese plate with cloudberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle in January means icy roads — private 4WD vehicle with experienced driver strongly recommended. Dress in full winter gear including crampons/ice grippers for walking near Geysir and Gullfoss. Approximately 6–7 hours round trip from the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a late resort breakfast. Morning at leisure — read by the fire in the resort lounge, enjoy the indoor heated pool, or book an additional spa treatment. Optional yoga or meditation class if offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak — travel to Flúðir village to experience Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool dating to 1891. Soak in the naturally heated 38–40°C spring water surrounded by geothermal activity, steam vents, and a small geyser. A more intimate and authentic alternative to the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (second outing) — maximizing aurora sighting opportunities with a second dedicated jeep tour. January offers some of Iceland's best aurora conditions with long, dark nights. Guides will venture to the best viewing spots based on real-time cloud and aurora forecasts.

meals.breakfast: Late resort breakfast — Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with whipped cream and crowberry jam, smoked lamb, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Secret Lagoon's café in Flúðir — traditional Icelandic lamb soup and fresh rye bread with butter
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friðheimar Tomato Farm Restaurant (near Reykholt) — unique greenhouse dining experience with tomato-based cuisine, fresh tomato soup, and Bloody Marys made from house-grown tomatoes

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon is approximately 1.5 hours from the resort — private 4WD transfer recommended. Friðheimar requires advance reservations. The Northern Lights tour departs late evening — plan dinner accordingly to return to the resort by midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury glacier walk on Sólheimajökull glacier — equipped with crampons, helmets, and expert guides, explore the ice formations, crevasses, and blue ice caves of this accessible glacier tongue. A breathtaking and unique winter experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the South Coast — visit the dramatic black sand beach at Reynisfjara (with its iconic basalt column formations and Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and the picturesque village of Vík. Explore the Dyrhólaey promontory for panoramic coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort along the South Coast. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet, indulgent evening — private in-room dining with a curated Icelandic tasting menu, a bottle of premium Icelandic birch schnapps, and a beachfront fire pit session (if available at the resort).

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — hearty Icelandic porridge (hafragrautur) with brown sugar and butter, smoked fish platter, and strong Icelandic coffee for the glacier day ahead
meals.lunch: Lunch in Vík — Black Beach Restaurant for Icelandic fish and chips, langoustine soup, and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Private in-room fine dining experience arranged by the resort — surf and turf with Icelandic lobster tail and lamb rack, chocolate lava cake, and Icelandic dessert wines

day_by_day.notes: Glacier walk requires moderate fitness — wear waterproof clothing and sturdy boots (crampons provided). South Coast drive is approximately 2–2.5 hours from the resort. January road conditions can be challenging — private 4WD with driver essential. Reynisfjara beach has dangerous sneaker waves — stay behind the safety line.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day — indulge in the resort's spa facilities. Book a signature 90-minute geothermal hot stone massage and a Nordic body scrub using volcanic ash and sea salt. Enjoy the resort's private hot tub and sauna overlooking the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike — trek through Iceland's dramatic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains (note: January access may be limited due to snow; confirm with guides for winter accessibility). If accessible, experience the legendary natural hot spring pool surrounded by snow-dusted obsidian lava fields and colorful mountains. If highland roads are closed, substitute with a private snowmobile tour on a nearby glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory mid-trip dinner at the resort's chef's table — an exclusive 8-course tasting experience prepared personally by the head chef using seasonal Icelandic ingredients, paired with premium Icelandic and international wines.

meals.breakfast: Spa day breakfast — light and nourishing: Icelandic skyr with granola and berries, green smoothies, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Healthy resort lunch at the spa café — smoked salmon avocado bowls, Icelandic flatbread with hummus, and sparkling water with Icelandic herbs
meals.dinner: Exclusive 8-course chef's table experience at the resort — amuse-bouche of smoked trout roe, langoustine bisque, reindeer tartare, Arctic char with dill beurre blanc, Icelandic lamb three ways, artisan cheese course, skyr panna cotta, and petit fours

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar is typically inaccessible by standard vehicles in January due to snow and ice — a specialized super-jeep tour is required. Confirm availability at least 48 hours in advance with the resort concierge. The chef's table experience should be reserved upon arrival or before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private snowmobile adventure on Langjökull glacier — Iceland's second-largest glacier offers an exhilarating snowmobile experience with panoramic views of the Highland interior. Alternatively, explore the Into the Glacier ice tunnel for an underground glacial experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the geothermal valley of Haukadalur and the surrounding hot spring fields. Explore the lesser-visited Deildartunguhver — Europe's most powerful hot spring — and the historic Reykholt area associated with medieval scholar Snorri Sturluson.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy cocktails at the resort bar — Icelandic gin and tonic with crowberries, followed by a casual dinner. Check aurora forecast with the concierge for a potential spontaneous Northern Lights viewing from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Icelandic spread with fresh-baked rye bread, smoked lamb, Icelandic butter, skyr, and hot coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Krauma Geothermal Baths & Restaurant near Deildartunguhver — Icelandic lamb stew and freshly baked bread in a cozy geothermal setting
meals.dinner: Casual resort dinner — Icelandic fish stew (plokkfiskur), sourdough bread, and Icelandic craft beers from Ölvisholt Brugghús brewery

day_by_day.notes: Langjökull snowmobile tours require advance booking and a valid driver's license. Minimum age and fitness requirements apply. Into the Glacier tunnel tours are available year-round and offer a unique alternative. Krauma Baths can be combined with a short soak after lunch.

day_by_day.morning: Private whale watching tour from Reykjavik harbor — January offers chances to spot humpback whales, minke whales, and harbor porpoises. Luxury small-group boat with heated cabin, binoculars, and expert marine biologist guide. Dress in full thermal gear provided by the operator.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for an afternoon of culture — visit the Perlan Museum (Wonders of Iceland exhibition with a real indoor ice cave) and the Settlement Exhibition (871±2) showcasing Viking-age archaeological remains beneath the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Reykjavik at one of the city's premier restaurants, followed by a private Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (third outing) for one final dedicated aurora chase before the trip concludes.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure to Reykjavik — smoked salmon bagels, Icelandic yogurt, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Post-whale watching lunch at Kopar Restaurant at Reykjavik Old Harbour — Icelandic seafood platter with langoustine, scallops, and Arctic char, with harbor views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Óx Restaurant (Reykjavik's intimate 12-seat tasting menu restaurant) — avant-garde New Nordic cuisine with local Icelandic ingredients and premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January is weather-dependent — tours may be cancelled in rough seas. Luxury operators offer complimentary rebooking. Óx Restaurant has very limited seating and requires advance reservation months ahead — concierge must book immediately. Northern Lights jeep tour departs ~21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort — sleep in after the late Northern Lights tour. Enjoy a late brunch at the resort and a final morning soak in the private hot tub with beachfront views. Pack for any upcoming excursions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter tour over Iceland's volcanic landscape — fly over the Reykjanes Peninsula, volcanic craters, geothermal fields, and coastal cliffs. If budget allows, extend the flight over the Golden Circle or the South Coast glaciers for aerial photography. Approximately 45–90 minutes depending on package.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort — enjoy the sauna, steam room, and hot pool facilities. Light evening meal followed by stargazing and Northern Lights watch from the private beachfront with warm blankets and hot drinks provided by the resort.

meals.breakfast: Late resort brunch — eggs any style, Icelandic waffles, smoked fish, fresh pastries, and mimosas with Icelandic crowberry juice
meals.lunch: Light pre-helicopter snack at the resort — Icelandic cheese and charcuterie board with rye crackers and cloudberry jam
meals.dinner: Intimate resort dinner — Icelandic lobster (humar) bisque, pan-seared Arctic char with dill cream sauce, and skyr cheesecake with blueberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours must be booked well in advance and are weather-dependent. January conditions can cause last-minute cancellations — have a backup activity planned (e.g., additional spa time or a private photography workshop). Confirm with the resort if beachfront fire pits or outdoor heating are available for evening stargazing.

day_by_day.morning: Private photography tour with a professional Icelandic landscape photographer — explore the Reykjanes Peninsula's dramatic volcanic coastline, geothermal fields, and the Bridge Between Continents (Leif the Lucky Bridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates). Perfect for capturing Iceland's raw winter beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gunnuhver geothermal area on the Reykjanes Peninsula — dramatic boiling mud pools and steam vents. Explore the Reykjanes Lighthouse and the rugged coastal cliffs. Return to the resort for a relaxing afternoon in the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-suite Northern Lights dinner experience — the resort sets up a private outdoor heated terrace or glass-ceiling suite (if available) for aurora viewing while dining. Alternatively, a final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep for any remaining aurora enthusiasts in the group.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Icelandic oatmeal with caramelized apples, smoked trout, fresh rye bread, and Icelandic herbal tea
meals.lunch: Packed luxury picnic hamper from the resort — thermos of lamb soup, smoked lamb sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate, and hot coffee enjoyed at a scenic coastal viewpoint on the Reykjanes Peninsula
meals.dinner: Private romantic in-suite or terrace dinner — lobster thermidor, Wagyu beef with Icelandic mushroom sauce, truffle mashed potatoes, and a bottle of vintage Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Professional photography tour is approximately 4–5 hours — book through the resort concierge or a specialist Icelandic photography tour company. January light on the Reykjanes Peninsula offers stunning golden-hour photography even at midday (sun stays low on the horizon). Confirm the in-suite dining experience 24 hours in advance with the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — morning at complete leisure. Enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Take a final beachfront walk to collect memories and photographs of the Icelandic coastline in winter. Optional: book a final 60-minute spa treatment as a send-off treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Blue Lagoon for a second visit — this time choosing the exclusive Retreat Spa package (if not done on Day 2) for the ultimate luxury experience including private changing suite, in-water floating massage, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lounge with panoramic lava field views. A perfect final afternoon in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort — a special send-off meal arranged by the concierge. Toast to the trip with Icelandic brennivín (Black Death schnapps) and a curated selection of Icelandic craft spirits. Early evening to allow for packing and preparation for departure.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — the full Icelandic luxury spread: smoked salmon, skyr, Icelandic cheeses, fresh pastries, waffles, eggs, and premium coffee and juices
meals.lunch: Moss Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon Retreat — Iceland's most exclusive geothermal dining experience with panoramic lava field views, featuring a seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort — Icelandic lamb rack with rosemary and thyme, roasted root vegetables, and a decadent chocolate and skyr dessert tower, paired with an Icelandic wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon Retreat package is the most exclusive tier — book months in advance as availability is extremely limited. Ensure all luggage is packed this evening for an efficient morning departure. The resort concierge should arrange the airport transfer for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort — enjoy a last Icelandic breakfast and check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Keflavik International Airport. Allow ample time for check-in and security (recommended: arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights).
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Browse the airport's duty-free for Icelandic souvenirs — Icelandic wool products, Skyr beauty products, Icelandic sea salt, brennivín, and Icelandic chocolates. Board your flight home carrying memories of Iceland's Northern Lights, hot springs, glaciers, and extraordinary landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — light and easy: skyr with granola, fresh fruit, and Icelandic coffee before checkout
meals.lunch: Airport dining at Keflavik — Icelandic lamb soup or smoked salmon bagel at one of the airport's restaurants before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at final destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer the evening before departure. Check flight status and allow extra time in January due to potential weather delays. Keflavik Airport has excellent duty-free shopping — budget extra time if planning to purchase souvenirs. Ensure all Icelandic purchases (wool, spirits) comply with airline baggage regulations. Consider a final aurora check at the airport parking area if departing late — Keflavik's surroundings can offer aurora views on clear nights.

query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026
